Vendor Profile

F5 Networks

Application delivery, load balancing, web application security, and API protection – deployed on hardware appliances, software, and as cloud-delivered SaaS.

Networking Security

Overview

F5 Networks is the market leader in application delivery controllers (ADCs) – the technology that sits in front of applications and services to distribute traffic, manage TLS termination, enforce access policies, and protect against web-based attacks. Its BIG-IP platform is deployed in the majority of large enterprise and public sector environments as the primary layer for application availability, performance, and security. F5 also develops NGINX, one of the world's most widely deployed web servers and proxy technologies, and operates a growing cloud-delivered SaaS portfolio called F5 Distributed Cloud Services.

In a customer environment, F5 typically sits at the edge of the data centre or cloud perimeter, in front of web applications, APIs, and internal services. It handles SSL/TLS offload, intelligent load balancing, DDoS mitigation, and web application firewall (WAF) policy enforcement. The Access Policy Manager (APM) module adds a network access and identity layer, enabling Zero Trust network access (ZTNA) and VPN replacement scenarios. F5's SSL Orchestrator product chains together third-party inspection tools – security appliances can be inserted into the decrypted traffic path without individual integration work.

Arrow ECS UK's F5 relationship is one of the highest-volume vendor relationships in the phase 1 group, with over 2,400 transaction lines in 2025. The book is dominated by BIG-IP hardware appliances (the rSeries platform), software licences, support renewals (F5 Global Support), and Enterprise Licensing Agreements – confirming F5 as a large, renewal-heavy account with a mature installed base.

Arrow-Carried Portfolio

All products below are confirmed in Arrow ECS UK's 2025 sales data unless otherwise noted.

BIG-IP rSeries Appliances
F5's current-generation hardware ADC platform. The r4600, r5800, r5900, r5920, r10600, r10900, and r12600 models all appear in Arrow's 2025 sales data. Deployed on-premises in front of applications for traffic management, SSL offload, WAF, and access control.
Hardware ADC On-premises
BIG-IP Local Traffic Manager (LTM)
The core load balancing and traffic management module. Distributes application traffic across server pools, performs health monitoring, and handles SSL/TLS termination. Present across virtually every BIG-IP deployment.
Load balancing TLS termination High availability
BIG-IP Advanced WAF
Web application firewall that protects against OWASP Top 10 threats, automated attacks, and API abuse. The Advanced WAF module adds bot defence and behavioural analytics beyond the standard WAF capability. Confirmed in Arrow 2025 sales data.
WAF API security Bot defence
BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM)
Identity and access control module that enables Zero Trust network access, VPN, and SSO. APM integrates with identity providers and can enforce device compliance checks (including via OPSWAT MetaAccess) before granting access to protected resources.
ZTNA VPN replacement SSO
BIG-IP SSL Orchestrator
Decrypts SSL/TLS traffic and routes it through a chain of third-party inspection tools (IDS, sandbox, DLP, etc.) before re-encrypting and forwarding. Solves the problem of encrypted traffic bypassing security controls. Supports integration with HSMs for key management.
SSL inspection Security chaining HSM integration
BIG-IP Virtual Edition
Software-based BIG-IP deployed as a virtual machine in VMware, KVM, or public cloud environments. Provides the same LTM, WAF, and APM functionality as hardware appliances. Subscription licensing confirmed in Arrow 2025 data.
Virtual Cloud-ready Subscription
VELOS Chassis
F5's high-capacity chassis platform for large-scale data centres. The VELOS CX410 chassis with BX110 blades is confirmed in Arrow's 2025 sales data – suited to telco, financial services, and large enterprise environments requiring carrier-grade throughput.
Chassis High capacity Data centre
F5 Distributed Cloud Services
SaaS-delivered application security and delivery platform. Includes cloud WAF, API security, DDoS protection, and managed edge services. The Managed Service Standard tier is confirmed in Arrow 2025 data, indicating active SaaS adoption alongside traditional hardware.
SaaS WAF DDoS

Cross-sell & Expansion Opportunities

OPSWAT
Zero Trust Access – Endpoint Compliance via MetaAccess
OPSWAT MetaAccess integrates directly with F5 BIG-IP APM. When a user attempts to access an APM-protected resource, MetaAccess can be invoked to verify device compliance – OS patch level, AV status, disk encryption – before access is granted. This brings device health into the F5 access policy without requiring a separate endpoint agent or NAC infrastructure. Particularly relevant in healthcare, government, and regulated finance environments deploying Zero Trust.
Entrust
HSM Key Protection for F5 SSL Orchestrator
F5 BIG-IP and SSL Orchestrator support integration with network-attached HSMs for private key storage and SSL/TLS operations. Entrust nShield HSMs can serve as the hardware root of trust for F5's certificate keys – ensuring private keys never exist in software and meeting FIPS 140-2 Level 3 requirements. This is a natural expansion in any F5 SSL Orchestrator or high-assurance WAF deployment where key protection is a compliance requirement.
Black Duck
SDLC Security Upstream of Runtime Protection
F5 protects applications at runtime – blocking web attacks, malformed requests, and API abuse at the network edge. Black Duck identifies vulnerabilities in the application's code and open-source dependencies before it is deployed. The two address different parts of the application security lifecycle: Black Duck prevents vulnerable code reaching production; F5 mitigates exploitation of whatever reaches the edge. In any F5 WAF conversation with organisations that have an internal development function, Black Duck is a natural adjacent discussion.
IBM Security
F5 WAF & APM Events into IBM QRadar
F5 BIG-IP ASM (WAF) and APM generate detailed security event logs. IBM QRadar can ingest F5 syslog feeds to correlate web application attacks with identity and network events in the SOC. This is particularly useful for customers running both F5 for application delivery and IBM QRadar for security operations – the F5 telemetry adds an application-layer visibility dimension that network-only SIEM inputs cannot provide.

Competitive Landscape

Vendors you are likely to encounter on the same shortlist. F5 is the established incumbent in most enterprise ADC accounts.

Citrix (NetScaler)
ADC / Load Balancing
Citrix NetScaler (now NetScaler by Cloud Software Group) is F5's primary ADC competitor. NetScaler has historically been stronger in Citrix-centric environments (Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops). F5 leads on feature depth for complex application delivery policies, multi-cloud deployment flexibility, and security integration breadth. Many large enterprises run both vendors in different parts of the estate.
Kemp (Progress)
ADC / Load Balancing
Kemp (acquired by Progress) competes with F5 in the mid-market load balancing segment. Kemp's pricing is significantly lower and its platform is simpler. F5 wins on feature depth, security integration, and enterprise-scale reliability. Kemp is typically encountered in smaller organisations or in non-critical application tiers within larger ones.
Cloudflare
Cloud WAF / DDoS / CDN
Cloudflare competes with F5 Distributed Cloud Services in cloud-delivered WAF, DDoS, and API security. Cloudflare's reverse-proxy model is simpler to deploy for internet-facing applications. F5 wins when organisations need on-premises control, deep customisation, or integration with existing BIG-IP infrastructure. Many organisations run F5 on-premises and Cloudflare at the edge simultaneously.
Palo Alto Networks (Prisma)
ZTNA / Application Security
Palo Alto Prisma Access competes with F5 APM in Zero Trust network access and VPN replacement. Palo Alto leads on cloud-native SASE architecture; F5 leads in organisations with heavy on-premises investment in BIG-IP infrastructure. The two are increasingly positioned in the same Zero Trust and hybrid access conversations.

Ideal Customer Profile

Organisation Size
Mid-market to large enterprise and government. BIG-IP hardware suits organisations running complex multi-application environments. Virtual Edition and Distributed Cloud scale down to smaller deployments.
Verticals
Financial services, government, healthcare, telco, and large retail. Broadly sector-agnostic – any organisation with web-facing applications or internal services requiring high availability, secure access, and WAF protection.
Trigger Events
BIG-IP hardware refresh (rSeries migration from VIPRION / older chassis); SSL certificate management project; WAF deployment for PCI DSS or ISO 27001; Zero Trust network access initiative; DDoS incident; API security programme.
Key Personas
Head of Network / Infrastructure, Security Architect, CISO (for WAF and ZTNA conversations), Application Owner (for ADC performance), and IT Procurement for ELA and renewal discussions.
